records.literal_gloss: And it was in year four of Darius the king, came [the] word of Yahweh to Zechariah, on the fourth of the month the ninth, in Kislev.

en.L: And it came about in the fourth year of Darius the king that the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah on the fourth of the ninth month, in Kislev.
en.B: In the fourth year of King Darius's reign, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah. It was the fourth day of Kislev, the ninth month.
en.R: In Darius's fourth year as king, on the fourth day of Kislev, the ninth month of the year, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave a message to Zechariah.

fr.L: Et il arriva, la quatrième année du roi Darius, que la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée à Zacharie, le quatrième [jour] du neuvième mois, en Kislev.
fr.B: La quatrième année du règne du roi Darius, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée à Zacharie. C’était le quatrième jour de Kislev, le neuvième mois.
fr.R: La quatrième année où Darius était roi, le quatrième jour de Kislev, le neuvième mois de l’année, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné un message à Zacharie.

es.L: Y sucedió que en el año cuarto del rey Darío vino la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a Zacarías, el día cuarto del mes noveno, en Quisleu.

es.R: En el cuarto año de Darío como rey, el cuarto día de Quisleu, el noveno mes del año, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio un mensaje a Zacarías.

vi.L: Vào năm thứ tư đời vua Đa-ri-út, lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với Xa-cha-ri vào ngày mồng bốn tháng thứ chín, tức tháng Kít-lêu.

ko.B: 다리오가 다스린 지 4년째 되는 해에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 스가랴에게 임했다. 그날은 아홉째 달인 기슬르 월 나흗날이었다.

decisions.choice: the fourth day of the ninth month, Kislev, in Darius's fourth year: early December 518 BC
decisions.reason: This is nearly two years after the night visions (1:7) and about halfway through the rebuilding of the temple, which was finished in Darius's sixth year (Ezra 6:15). Kislev is the Babylonian name of the ninth month, used also in Nehemiah 1:1. The modern date is worked out from the Babylonian calendar.

decisions.choice: Zechariah is named in the third person
decisions.reason: As in 1:1 and 1:7, a heading speaks of the prophet by name. Chapters 7-8 hold the prophet's answer to a question about fasting, given in several messages (7:4, 8; 8:1, 18).

decisions.choice: in the fourth year of Darius the king (L); of King Darius's reign (B); in Darius's fourth year as king (R)
decisions.reason: The dated heading follows the wording of 1:1 at each level. Here the Hebrew calls Darius "the king". Readable puts the date first and says "of the year" for the month, without converting to the modern calendar.

decisions.choice: The dated narrative of 7:1-3: passé simple at L and B ("fut adressée", "avait envoyé"), passé composé at R ("a donné"); the LORD's answer from 7:4 is speech and uses the tenses of speech at every level
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for the dated headings and narrative frames of Haggai and Zechariah.

decisions.choice: "la quatrième année du roi Darius" (L), "du règne du roi Darius" (B), "où Darius était roi" (R); "Kislev" as Nehemiah 1:1
decisions.reason: The date formula as the term sheet, with no modern calendar in the text; the meaning decision's footnote gives the modern date.

decisions.choice: "en el año cuarto del rey Darío" (L); "en el cuarto año del reinado de Darío" (B); "en el cuarto año de Darío como rey" (R); "Quisleu"
decisions.reason: Dated headings follow the term sheet's Haggai and Zechariah pattern at each level; the month's name is "Quisleu", as in Nehemiah 1:1 in Spanish.

decisions.choice: "katika mwaka wa nne wa mfalme Dario" (L); "wa utawala wa Dario" (B); "wa Dario kuwa mfalme" (R); "Kislevu"
decisions.reason: The dated heading as the term sheet and the published Haggai 1:1; "Kislevu" is the month's published form in Nehemiah 1:1.

decisions.choice: "다리오 왕 제4년" (L); "다리오가 다스린 지 4년째 되는 해" (B); "다리오가 왕이 된 지 4년째 되는 해" (R); "기슬르 월"
decisions.reason: The Kings formula for dated headings, as the term sheet and Haggai 1:1; Kislev is "기슬르 월" as in Nehemiah 1:1. Readable gives the day in figures, as Haggai 1:1 R does.

decisions.choice: dated heading "năm thứ tư đời vua Đa-ri-út" (L) / "triều vua Đa-ri-út" (B) / "Đa-ri-út làm vua" (R); "ngày mồng bốn"; Kislev as "Kít-lêu"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's pattern for Haggai and Zechariah; days one to ten take "mồng". "Kít-lêu" is the published form (Nehemiah 1:1). No level converts to a modern date; the meaning decision gives it.

ko.L: 벧엘이 사레셀과 레겜멜렉과 그의 사람들을 보내어 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 은혜를 구하게 하였는데,
ko.B: 벧엘 사람들이 사레셀과 레겜멜렉과 그 일행을 보내어 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 은혜를 구하게 했다.

decisions.choice: Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-melech: the town of Bethel sent two men with their companions
alternatives: Bethel-sharezer sent Regem-melech and his men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be divided in more than one way. Bethel may be the subject, the town standing for its people, as cities often do. Or "Bethel-sharezer" may be one man's name, a Babylonian-style name formed with the name of a god, and he sent Regem-melech. A few take Bethel as the place to which the men were sent, but the question is put to the priests of the temple in Jerusalem (verse 3). The translation takes the first reading.

decisions.choice: Bethel: a town north of Jerusalem, resettled after the exile; Sharezer: a Babylonian name
decisions.reason: Bethel lay about twelve miles north of Jerusalem, and people of Bethel were among those who returned (Ezra 2:28; Nehemiah 7:32). Sharezer is a name of Babylonian form (compare 2 Kings 19:37), and Regem-melech may mean "friend of the king"; such names suggest men born in the exile.

decisions.choice: to entreat the favor of the LORD: to pray to the LORD and seek his goodwill
decisions.reason: The phrase, literally "to soften the face", means to seek someone's favor (Exodus 32:11; Malachi 1:9). The delegation comes to worship and to ask a question.

decisions.choice: The people of Bethel (B, R); their men (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the people of" for the town, as m1 reads it, and "their men" for the companions of the two. Readable says what entreating the LORD's favor means. The sentence runs on into verse 3, so Literal ends with a comma.

decisions.choice: "apaiser la face du SEIGNEUR" (L), "implorer la faveur" (B)
decisions.reason: French idiom for entreating someone's favour; Literal keeps "la face".

decisions.choice: "Sarézer", "Reguem-mélec"
decisions.reason: The two names follow the term sheet (uncertain); Betel is the published form. B and R say "the people of Bethel", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Shareza", "Regem-meleki"
decisions.reason: "Shareza" is the published Swahili form of the same name (2 Kings 19:37); "Regem-meleki" is new, formed by the usual pattern (final vowel added, as "Ebed-meleki").

decisions.choice: "벧엘 사람들" (B), "벧엘 성읍 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: the town sends the men (meaning decision); Literal keeps "벧엘이".

decisions.choice: "Sa-rết-xe", "Rê-ghem-Mê-léc"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms; "Mê-léc" for melech as in "Ê-bết-Mê-léc" (Jeremiah 38:7).

ko.L: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집에 있는 제사장들과 예언자들에게 말하게 하였다. "제가 여러 해 동안 해 온 것처럼, 다섯째 달에 몸을 삼가며 울어야 합니까?"

ko.R: 그들은 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전에 있는 제사장들과 예언자들에게 물어야 했다. "저희가 여러 해 동안 해 온 것처럼, 다섯째 달에 계속 슬퍼하며 금식해야 합니까?"

decisions.choice: the fifth month: the fast that mourned the burning of the temple
decisions.reason: In the fifth month of 586 BC, the Babylonian commander burned the temple, the king's palace and the houses of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:8-9; Jeremiah 52:12-13). The exiles mourned the day with a fast. Now that the temple was being rebuilt, the people of Bethel asked whether the fast should go on. The answer comes at the end of chapter 8 (8:19), after the LORD has spoken about the heart of the matter.

decisions.choice: keeping myself apart: abstaining, keeping a fast
decisions.reason: The verb means to set oneself apart, and is related to the word for a Nazirite, who abstained from wine (Numbers 6:2-3). Here it means holding back from food and pleasures in mourning.

decisions.choice: I: the town speaks as one person
decisions.reason: The delegation speaks for the people of Bethel, using "I" for the whole community, as Israel often does in the psalms.

decisions.choice: we (R); mourning and fasting (B, R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "we", since the whole community asks. Balanced and Readable give "keeping myself apart" as "fasting" (m2), and "weep" as "weeping" (B) or "mourning" (R). The priests "who belong to" the house are the priests "of" the house.

decisions.choice: "apartándome" (L); "ayunando" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means keeping oneself apart in a fast; L keeps the image, B and R name the fast. R speaks for the town with "we", as the English R does.

decisions.choice: The town asks the priests in 합쇼체 with "제가" (L, B) and "저희가" (R)
decisions.reason: The question is put to priests and prophets, so it is polite; the town speaks as one person (meaning decision), and Readable makes it plural as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "tôi" (L, B) / "chúng tôi" (R): the town asks as one person
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the town speak as "I"; L and B keep it, R says "chúng tôi" as the English R does.

decisions.choice: the seventh month: the fast that mourned the murder of Gedaliah
decisions.reason: Jewish tradition connects a fast in the seventh month with the murder of Gedaliah, the governor the Babylonians set over Judah after the fall of Jerusalem; his death drove the last of the people to Egypt (2 Kings 25:25-26; Jeremiah 41:1-3). The Day of Atonement also falls in the seventh month (Leviticus 16:29), but it was commanded in the law, and the fasts here are fasts of mourning added in the exile. The connection with Gedaliah is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: these seventy years: since the fall of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: From 586 BC to this message in 518 BC was nearly seventy years, the time of judgment foretold by Jeremiah; see the note at 1:12.

decisions.choice: was it really for me: a question about motive, stressed by repeating "me"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the pronoun at the end, "for me, me?" The LORD asks whether their fasting was turned toward him, or was only grief for their own loss. Isaiah 58:3-7 asks the same of fasting without justice.

decisions.choice: for me ... for me (L); did you truly fast for me (B); were you really fasting for me (R); quotation marks
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated pronoun; Balanced and Readable show the stress with "truly" and "really". "Me" takes the setting for pronouns of God. The words Zechariah is to say are in double quotation marks, which close at the end of verse 7. Readable makes the long question a statement and a short question.

decisions.choice: The message Zechariah is told to deliver (7:5-7) takes no quotation marks
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for French: God's message that the prophet is sent to deliver is not quoted; the English quotes it.

decisions.choice: "por mí, por mí" (L); "por mí" (B, R)
decisions.reason: L keeps the repeated "me" that stresses the question; B and R say it once with "de verdad". The people are addressed in the plural, so the verbs take plural_you. God's speech is quoted here because Zechariah is told what to say, as the English does.

decisions.choice: God commands the prophet with the bare imperative "Hãy nói", and speaks to the people as "các ngươi" (rebuke)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's address: "các ngươi" to the people in rebuke at every level.

decisions.choice: "70년" in figures at every level, as in 1:12
decisions.reason: These are Jeremiah's seventy years of exile, which are written in figures at every level as a set phrase (1:12; 2 Chronicles 36:21), an exception to the rule that counts under a hundred in running text are in words (term sheet, numbers).

records.literal_gloss: [Are] not the words which proclaimed Yahweh by [the] hand of the prophets the former, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, and its cities around it, and the Negev and the Shephelah inhabited?

en.L: Are not [these] the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} proclaimed by the hand of the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, and its cities around it, and the Negev and the Shephelah were inhabited?"
en.B: Are these not the very words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} proclaimed through the earlier prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous, along with the towns around it, and when people lived in the Negev and the Shephelah?"
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke these same words through the prophets of long ago. At that time people lived in Jerusalem, and it was doing well. People lived in the towns around it, in the Negev in the south and in the western foothills."

fr.B: Ne sont-ce pas là les paroles mêmes que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a proclamées par les prophètes d’autrefois, quand Jérusalem était habitée et prospère, avec les villes qui l’entouraient, et quand on habitait le Néguev et la Shéfela ?
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit ces mêmes paroles par les prophètes d’autrefois. À cette époque, Jérusalem était habitée et tout allait bien pour elle. Des gens vivaient dans les villes autour, dans le Néguev au sud et dans les collines de l’ouest.

es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo estas mismas palabras por medio de los profetas de hace mucho tiempo. En aquel tiempo había gente viviendo en Jerusalén, y a la ciudad le iba bien. También había gente en los pueblos de alrededor, en el Néguev, al sur, y en las colinas del oeste».

vi.L: Chẳng phải [đây là] những lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã công bố qua tay các nhà tiên tri thời trước, khi Giê-ru-sa-lem còn có người ở và được an ổn, cùng các thành chung quanh nó, và miền Nê-ghép và Sơ-phê-la còn có người ở sao?"

ko.L: 예루살렘과 그 주변의 성읍들에 사람이 살고 평안하였으며, 네겝과 스벨라에 사람이 살던 때에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이전 예언자들의 손을 통하여 외치신 말씀들이 [이것이] 아니냐?"

decisions.choice: are not these the words: the former prophets said the same
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "are not the words", leaving "these" to be understood. The LORD points to what the earlier prophets said about fasting and worship without justice (Isaiah 58:3-7; Jeremiah 14:12), which verses 9-10 sum up.

decisions.choice: at ease: safe and prosperous
decisions.reason: The word describes a settled, peaceful life (Jeremiah 49:31; Psalm 122:6-7). The prophets spoke when the land was full and thriving, and it was lost because the people did not listen.

decisions.choice: the Negev and the Shephelah: the dry south and the low hills to the west
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry country south of Judah's hills; the Shephelah is the band of low hills between the hill country and the coastal plain. With Jerusalem and its towns, they make up the whole of Judah.

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question (R); in the south; the western foothills (R)
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question means, and says where the Negev and the Shephelah were. The closing mark ends the words begun in verse 5.

decisions.choice: "le Néguev et la Shéfela" (L, B), "le Néguev au sud et les collines de l'ouest" (R)
decisions.reason: The names as the term sheet; Readable says where they are, as the English.

decisions.choice: "el Néguev y la Sefela" (L, B); "el Néguev, al sur, y las colinas del oeste" (R)
decisions.reason: Néguev and Sefela are the published forms (1 Samuel 27:10; 1 Kings 10:27); R explains them, as the English R does.

decisions.choice: "Negebu", "Shefela" (L, B); "Negebu upande wa kusini", "vilima vya magharibi" (R)
decisions.reason: The published Swahili forms (Jeremiah 17:26; 32:44); Readable explains them as the English does.

decisions.choice: "스벨라" (L); "서쪽 평지" (B); "서쪽 산기슭" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Jeremiah 17:26 at each level.

decisions.choice: the formula with Zechariah's name
decisions.reason: The formula keeps the wording set for the prophets, with the prophet named in place of "me".

source.text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר מִשְׁפַּ֤ט אֱמֶת֙ שְׁפֹ֔טוּ וְחֶ֣סֶד וְרַֽחֲמִ֔ים עֲשׂ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־אָחִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, saying: Justice of truth judge, and loyal love and compassion do, each with his brother,

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Judge with true justice, and practice loyal love and compassion {{gender:toward one another|each man toward his brother}};
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Judge with true justice. Show loyal love and compassion to one another.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Judge fairly and honestly. Show faithful love and compassion to one another.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Jugez [selon] un jugement de vérité, et pratiquez l’amour loyal et la compassion {{gender:les uns envers les autres|chacun envers son frère}} ;
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Rendez une justice vraie. Montrez-vous les uns aux autres un amour fidèle et de la compassion.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Jugez avec justice et honnêteté. Soyez pleins d’amour fidèle et de compassion les uns envers les autres.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: {{plural_you:Juzguen|Juzgad}} con juicio verdadero, y {{plural_you:practiquen|practicad}} el amor leal y la compasión {{gender:unos con otros|cada uno con su hermano}};
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: {{plural_you:Juzguen|Juzgad}} con verdadera justicia. {{plural_you:Muestren|Mostrad}} amor fiel y compasión unos a otros.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: {{plural_you:Juzguen|Juzgad}} con justicia y honradez. {{plural_you:Muestren|Mostrad}} amor fiel y compasión unos a otros.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này: Hãy xét xử theo công lý chân thật, và hãy thực hành tình yêu thương thành tín và lòng thương xót với nhau;
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán như vầy: Hãy xét xử theo công lý chân thật. Hãy tỏ tình yêu thương thành tín và lòng thương xót với nhau.
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán: Hãy xét xử cách công bằng và ngay thẳng. Hãy đối xử với nhau bằng tình thương không hề thay đổi và lòng thương xót.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Hukumuni kwa hukumu ya kweli, na tendeni upendo usiokoma na huruma kila mtu kwa ndugu yake;
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Hukumuni kwa haki ya kweli. Oneshaneni upendo usiokoma na huruma ninyi kwa ninyi.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Hukumuni kwa haki na kwa uaminifu. Oneshaneni upendo wa kweli na huruma ninyi kwa ninyi.

ko.L: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 참된 정의로 재판하고, 서로 한결같은 사랑과 긍휼을 베풀어라.
ko.B: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 참되고 바르게 재판하여라. 서로 한결같은 사랑과 긍휼을 베풀어라.
ko.R: 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 공정하고 정직하게 재판하여라. 서로 변함없는 사랑과 자비를 베풀어라.

decisions.choice: judge with true justice: give verdicts that are fair and can be trusted
decisions.reason: The words are addressed to all who settle disputes, from judges to elders at the town gate. "True" means faithful and reliable, a judgment that does not bend for a bribe or for the powerful (Ezekiel 18:8).

decisions.choice: loyal love and compassion: faithful kindness and tender mercy toward others
decisions.reason: *Hesed* is the loyal love that people bound together owe one another (see the note at Hosea 6:6). The second word is the compassion of a parent for a child (Psalm 103:13). The LORD asks his people to treat one another as he treats them.

decisions.choice: the message of the earlier prophets in a few words
decisions.reason: Justice, loyal love and care for the weak are the heart of the earlier prophets' call (Hosea 6:6; Amos 5:24; Micah 6:8; Jeremiah 7:5-6; 22:3). This, not fasting, is what the LORD asked.

decisions.choice: loyal love (L, B); faithful love (R); toward one another / each man toward his brother (L)
decisions.reason: *Hesed* follows the settled wording for the prophets. "Each man toward his brother" means everyone toward everyone, men and women alike, so Literal gives it the gender setting, and Balanced and Readable say "one another". The sentence runs on into verse 10, so Literal ends with a semicolon.

decisions.choice: ḥesed "amour loyal" (L), "amour fidèle" (B, R); "compassion" for rachamim
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and published Isaiah and the Psalms: French Balanced says "amour fidèle" where the English Balanced says "loyal love".

decisions.choice: {{gender:les uns envers les autres|chacun envers son frère}} (L)
decisions.reason: The same setting as the English Literal, in French words.

decisions.choice: "amor leal" (L); "amor fiel" (B, R); "compasión"
decisions.reason: Hesed follows the Spanish prophets at each level; rahamim is "compasión".

decisions.choice: unos con otros / cada uno con su hermano
decisions.reason: Spanish has the two wordings the English setting gives, so L keeps the gender span.

decisions.choice: "upendo usiokoma" for hesed (L, B); "upendo wa kweli" (R); "huruma" for rachamim
decisions.reason: The term sheet's key terms for hesed and rachamim. Readable follows the English "faithful love" with "upendo wa kweli".

decisions.choice: "kila mtu kwa ndugu yake" (L), with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Mtu" and "ndugu" include women and men, so the English gender setting has nothing to change; Balanced and Readable say "ninyi kwa ninyi" (one another).

decisions.choice: "한결같은 사랑과 긍휼" (L, B); "변함없는 사랑과 자비" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheets' words for hesed and rachamim. "서로" covers the English gender span ("each man toward his brother"), so Korean has none.

decisions.choice: hesed "tình yêu thương thành tín" (L, B) / "tình thương không hề thay đổi" (R); rachamim "lòng thương xót"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for hesed in the prophets; rachamim is kept apart as "lòng thương xót".

decisions.choice: "với nhau" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span for "each man toward his brother"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "với nhau" ("to one another") already includes everyone and has no second, male-only wording to offer.

source.text: וְאַלְמָנָ֧ה וְיָת֛וֹם גֵּ֥ר וְעָנִ֖י אַֽל־תַּעֲשֹׁ֑קוּ וְרָעַת֙ אִ֣ישׁ אָחִ֔יו אַֽל־תַּחְשְׁב֖וּ בִּלְבַבְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and widow and fatherless, sojourner and poor, do not oppress, and evil of each [against] his brother do not plan in your heart.

en.L: and do not oppress the widow and the fatherless, the sojourner and the poor; and do not devise evil in your hearts {{gender:against one another|each man against his brother}}.
en.B: Do not oppress the widow or the orphan, the outsider or the poor. And do not plot evil against one another in your hearts.
en.R: Do not mistreat widows, orphans, foreigners or poor people. Do not even think about how to harm one another.

fr.L: et n’opprimez pas la veuve et l’orphelin, l’étranger et le pauvre ; et ne méditez pas dans vos cœurs le mal {{gender:les uns contre les autres|chacun contre son frère}}.
fr.B: N’opprimez pas la veuve ni l’orphelin, l’immigré ni le pauvre. Et ne tramez pas dans vos cœurs le mal les uns contre les autres.
fr.R: Ne maltraitez pas les veuves, les orphelins, les étrangers ou les pauvres. Ne pensez même pas à faire du mal aux autres.

es.L: y no {{plural_you:opriman|oprimáis}} a la viuda ni al huérfano, al inmigrante ni al pobre; y no {{plural_you:tramen|traméis}} el mal en {{plural_you:su corazón|vuestro corazón}} {{gender:unos contra otros|cada uno contra su hermano}}.
es.B: No {{plural_you:opriman|oprimáis}} a la viuda ni al huérfano, al extranjero ni al pobre. Y no {{plural_you:tramen|traméis}} en {{plural_you:su corazón|vuestro corazón}} hacerse daño unos a otros.
es.R: No {{plural_you:maltraten|maltratéis}} a las viudas, a los huérfanos, a los extranjeros ni a los pobres. Ni siquiera {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} en cómo hacerse daño unos a otros.

vi.L: và đừng áp bức người góa bụa và kẻ mồ côi, người ngoại kiều và người nghèo khó; và đừng mưu tính điều ác trong lòng các ngươi để hại nhau.
vi.B: Đừng áp bức người góa bụa hay trẻ mồ côi, người ngoại kiều hay người nghèo. Cũng đừng ngấm ngầm mưu tính điều ác trong lòng để hại nhau.
vi.R: Đừng ức hiếp những người góa bụa, trẻ mồ côi, người nước ngoài hay người nghèo. Ngay cả trong ý nghĩ, cũng đừng tìm cách hại nhau.

sw.L: wala msimdhulumu mjane na yatima, mgeni na maskini; wala msiwaziane mabaya mioyoni mwenu kila mtu dhidi ya ndugu yake.
sw.B: Msimdhulumu mjane wala yatima, mgeni wala maskini. Wala msipange mioyoni mwenu kutendeana mabaya.
sw.R: Msiwatendee vibaya wajane, yatima, wageni wala maskini. Wala msifikirie hata kidogo jinsi ya kudhuruana.

ko.L: 과부와 고아와 나그네와 가난한 자를 억압하지 말고, 너희 마음속으로 서로 해칠 악을 꾀하지 마라.
ko.B: 과부나 고아, 나그네나 가난한 사람을 억누르지 마라. 마음속으로 서로 해칠 일을 꾀하지 마라.
ko.R: 과부와 고아와 외국인과 가난한 사람들을 괴롭히지 마라. 서로 해칠 생각조차 하지 마라.

decisions.choice: the widow, the fatherless, the sojourner and the poor: people with no one to protect them
decisions.reason: The law and the prophets name these four again and again (Exodus 22:20-23; Deuteronomy 24:17; Jeremiah 7:6; 22:3). A widow and a fatherless child had lost the man who stood up for them; a sojourner was a foreigner living in Israel without land or family; the poor had nothing to fall back on.

decisions.choice: devise evil in your hearts: plot harm in secret
decisions.reason: The "heart" is where plans are made. The command reaches behind deeds to intentions, which only God sees. 8:17 repeats it.

decisions.choice: the fatherless, the sojourner (L); the orphan, the outsider (B); orphans, foreigners (R)
decisions.reason: The words for the fatherless and the sojourner follow Jeremiah 22:3 at Literal and Balanced. Readable says "foreigners", the plainest word for someone living away from their own people. "Against one another" takes the gender setting at Literal, as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: "l'immigré" (B) for the sojourner
decisions.reason: As the English Balanced "outsider": someone settled among a people not his own; Literal and Readable keep "l'étranger".

decisions.choice: "huérfano"; "inmigrante" (L); "extranjero" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The sojourner is "inmigrante" at L and "extranjero" at B and R, as in Deuteronomy 10:18 and 14:29 in Spanish.

source.text: וַיְמָאֲנ֣וּ לְהַקְשִׁ֔יב וַיִּתְּנ֥וּ כָתֵ֖ף סֹרָ֑רֶת וְאָזְנֵיהֶ֖ם הִכְבִּ֥ידוּ מִשְּׁמֽוֹעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they refused to pay attention, and they gave a shoulder stubborn, and their ears they made heavy from hearing.

en.L: But they refused to pay attention, and they turned a stubborn shoulder, and they made their ears heavy so as not to hear.
en.B: But they refused to pay attention. They turned their shoulders away stubbornly and stopped up their ears so that they would not hear.
en.R: But your ancestors refused to listen. They stubbornly turned away and covered their ears so they could not hear.

fr.L: Mais ils ont refusé d’être attentifs, et ils ont présenté une épaule rebelle, et ils ont rendu leurs oreilles pesantes pour ne pas entendre.
fr.B: Mais ils ont refusé d’écouter. Ils ont tourné le dos avec obstination et se sont bouché les oreilles pour ne pas entendre.
fr.R: Mais vos ancêtres ont refusé d’écouter. Ils se sont détournés avec entêtement et se sont bouché les oreilles pour ne pas entendre.

es.L: Pero ellos rehusaron prestar atención, y volvieron un hombro rebelde, y endurecieron sus oídos para no oír.
es.B: Pero ellos se negaron a prestar atención. Se dieron la vuelta con terquedad y se taparon los oídos para no oír.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} se negaron a escuchar. Tercamente se dieron la vuelta y se taparon los oídos para no oír.

vi.L: Nhưng chúng không chịu lắng nghe, chúng đưa vai cứng cỏi ra, và làm cho tai mình nặng đi để khỏi nghe.
vi.B: Nhưng chúng không chịu lắng nghe. Chúng ương ngạnh quay vai đi và bịt tai lại để khỏi phải nghe.
vi.R: Nhưng tổ tiên các ngươi không chịu nghe. Họ bướng bỉnh quay lưng lại và bịt tai để khỏi nghe.

sw.L: Lakini walikataa kusikiliza, wakageuza bega la ukaidi, wakayafanya masikio yao mazito ili wasisikie.
sw.B: Lakini walikataa kusikiliza. Waligeuza mabega yao kwa ukaidi, wakaziba masikio yao ili wasisikie.
sw.R: Lakini babu zenu walikataa kusikiliza. Waligeuka kwa ukaidi, wakaziba masikio yao ili wasisikie.

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 귀 기울이기를 거절하고, 고집스럽게 어깨를 돌리고, 듣지 않으려고 자기 귀를 무겁게 하였다.
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 귀 기울이기를 거절했다. 고집스럽게 등을 돌리고, 듣지 않으려고 귀를 막았다.
ko.R: 그러나 너희 조상들은 듣기를 거절했다. 고집스럽게 등을 돌리고, 듣지 않으려고 귀를 막아 버렸다.

decisions.choice: a stubborn shoulder: like an ox that will not take the yoke
decisions.reason: The picture is of an animal pulling its shoulder away from the yoke (Nehemiah 9:29; Hosea 4:16). The ancestors would not submit to the LORD's word.

decisions.choice: they made their ears heavy: they made themselves deaf
decisions.reason: "Heavy" ears are ears that will not hear (Isaiah 6:10). The people chose not to listen.

decisions.choice: they: the ancestors, who heard the earlier prophets
decisions.reason: The verse continues the story of the generations before the exile, whose refusal led to their scattering (verse 14; compare 1:4).

decisions.choice: your ancestors (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, which the Hebrew leaves to the context.

decisions.choice: God's account of the past (7:11-14) in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé simple at L and B
decisions.reason: It is speech, the word of the LORD to Zechariah, so it takes the tenses of speech, as the term sheet sets for the oracles.

decisions.choice: "chúng" (L, B) for the disobedient ancestors / "họ" (R) after "tổ tiên các ngươi"
decisions.reason: The term sheet uses "chúng" for Israel under judgment; at R "tổ tiên các ngươi" is named, and "họ" reads more naturally for ancestors.

decisions.choice: "volvieron un hombro rebelde"; "endurecieron sus oídos"
decisions.reason: L keeps the images of the ox refusing the yoke and of heavy ears; B and R give their sense. R names the hearers' ancestors, with plural_you on "sus antepasados", as the English R says "your ancestors".

source.text: וְלִבָּ֞ם שָׂ֣מוּ שָׁמִ֗יר מִ֠שְּׁמוֹעַ אֶת־הַתּוֹרָ֤ה וְאֶת־הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֜ח יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ בְּרוּח֔וֹ בְּיַ֖ד הַנְּבִיאִ֣ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֑ים וַֽיְהִי֙ קֶ֣צֶף גָּד֔וֹל מֵאֵ֖ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And their heart they made diamond from hearing the instruction and the words which sent Yahweh of hosts by his Spirit by [the] hand of the prophets the former; and there was wrath great from Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: And they made their hearts [like] diamond, so as not to hear the instruction and the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts sent by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit by the hand of the former prophets; and great wrath came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: They made their hearts as hard as diamond so that they would not listen to the instruction and the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies had sent by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit through the earlier prophets. So great wrath came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: They made their hearts as hard as rock so they would not listen to the teaching and the messages that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies had sent by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit through the prophets of long ago. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies became very angry.

fr.L: Et ils ont rendu leur cœur [dur comme le] diamant pour ne pas entendre la loi et les paroles que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées envoyait par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Esprit, par la main des anciens prophètes ; et une grande colère est venue {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Ils ont rendu leur cœur dur comme le diamant pour ne pas écouter l’instruction et les paroles que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées avait envoyées par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Esprit, par les prophètes d’autrefois. Alors une grande colère est venue {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: Ils ont rendu leur cœur dur comme la pierre pour ne pas écouter l’enseignement et les messages que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées avait envoyés par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Esprit, par les prophètes d’autrefois. Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}est mis très en colère.

es.L: Y pusieron su corazón [como] diamante, para no oír la instrucción y las palabras que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos enviaba por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Espíritu por medio de los profetas anteriores; y vino gran furor de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Endurecieron su corazón como el diamante para no escuchar la instrucción ni las palabras que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos había enviado por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Espíritu por medio de los profetas de antes. Por eso vino gran furor de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: Endurecieron su corazón como una piedra para no escuchar la enseñanza ni los mensajes que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos había enviado por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Espíritu por medio de los profetas de hace mucho tiempo. Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos se enojó mucho.

vi.L: Chúng làm cho lòng mình [như] kim cương, để khỏi nghe luật pháp và những lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai đến bởi Thần Linh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} qua tay các nhà tiên tri thời trước; và cơn thịnh nộ lớn đã đến từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân.
vi.B: Chúng làm cho lòng mình cứng như kim cương để khỏi nghe luật pháp và những lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai đến bởi Thần Linh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} qua các nhà tiên tri thời trước. Vì vậy, cơn thịnh nộ lớn đã đến từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân.
vi.R: Họ làm cho lòng mình cứng như đá để khỏi nghe lời dạy dỗ và các sứ điệp mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã gửi đến bởi Thần Linh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} qua các nhà tiên tri thời xưa. Vì vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã nổi giận rất lớn.

ko.L: 그들은 자기 마음을 금강석[처럼] 만들어, 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 영으로 이전 예언자들의 손을 통하여 보내신 가르침과 말씀들을 듣지 않았다. 그래서 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로부터 큰 진노가 내렸다.
ko.B: 그들은 마음을 금강석처럼 굳게 하여, 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 영으로 이전 예언자들을 통하여 보내신 가르침과 말씀을 듣지 않았다. 그래서 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로부터 큰 진노가 내렸다.
ko.R: 그들은 마음을 돌처럼 굳게 하여, 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 영으로 오래전 예언자들을 통하여 보내신 가르침과 말씀을 듣지 않았다. 그래서 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 몹시 분노하셨다.

decisions.choice: diamond: the hardest stone
decisions.reason: The word names a very hard stone, used as the point of an engraving tool (Jeremiah 17:1) and as a picture of a hard forehead (Ezekiel 3:9). Whether it was diamond, emery or flint, the point is the same: their hearts could not be marked.

decisions.choice: the instruction: God's law and teaching
decisions.reason: The word is *torah*, God's instruction, which the prophets called the people back to.

decisions.choice: by his Spirit through the former prophets: the prophets spoke by God's Spirit
decisions.reason: The words the prophets spoke were sent by the LORD through his Spirit. Nehemiah 9:30 says the same: "you warned them by your Spirit through your prophets."

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B); teaching (R); Spirit, capitalized; as hard as rock (R)
decisions.reason: *Torah* follows the wording set in Isaiah. The Spirit is God's Spirit, so it is capitalized, and "his" takes the setting for pronouns of God. Readable says "rock", a common picture of hardness.

decisions.choice: "instrucción" (L, B); "enseñanza" (R); "diamante" (L, B); "piedra" (R)
decisions.reason: Torah follows the Spanish prophets (instrucción / enseñanza); the hard stone is "diamante", as in Ezekiel 3:9 and Jeremiah 17:1 in Spanish. "Espíritu" is capitalized.

decisions.choice: "mafundisho" for torah at every level
decisions.reason: Here torah is the teaching sent through the prophets; the English has "instruction" / "teaching", and the Swahili notes give "mafundisho" at Balanced and Readable. Literal follows, since "sheria" would point to the written law alone.

decisions.choice: "그분의 영"
decisions.reason: God's Spirit is "영" with the honorific in these books (term sheet), not the New Testament "성령".

decisions.choice: torah "luật pháp" (L, B) / "lời dạy dỗ" (R); "Thần Linh của Ngài"
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "Thần Linh" for God's Spirit in the Old Testament, as Isaiah does.

decisions.choice: torah "la loi" (L), "l'instruction" (B), "l'enseignement" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for God's torah in the prophets.

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י כַאֲשֶׁר־קָרָ֖א וְלֹ֣א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ כֵּ֤ן יִקְרְאוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א אֶשְׁמָ֔ע אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, just as he called and not they listened, so they will call and not I will listen, says Yahweh of hosts,

en.L: And just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: Just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} called to them, but they would not listen. So when they called out, I would not listen, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

fr.L: Et il est arrivé que, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appelait et qu’ils n’ont pas écouté, ainsi ils ont appelé et je n’ai pas écouté, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appelait et qu’ils n’ont pas voulu écouter, de même ils ont appelé et je n’ai pas voulu écouter, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les appelait, mais ils n’ont pas voulu écouter. Alors, quand ils ont appelé au secours, je n’ai pas voulu écouter, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.

es.L: Y sucedió que, así como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} llamó y ellos no escucharon, así ellos llamaron y yo no escuché, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Así como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} llamó y ellos no quisieron escuchar, así ellos llamaron y yo no quise escuchar, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los llamó, pero ellos no quisieron escuchar. Por eso, cuando ellos clamaron, yo no quise escuchar, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

vi.L: Và như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã gọi mà chúng không nghe, thì chúng kêu gọi, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng không nghe, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.B: Như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã gọi mà chúng không chịu nghe, thì khi chúng kêu cầu, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng không nghe, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã gọi họ, nhưng họ không chịu nghe. Vì vậy khi họ kêu cầu, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng không nghe, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.

sw.L: Na ikawa, kama vile {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyoita, nao hawakusikiliza, ndivyo walivyoita, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} sikusikiliza, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Kama vile {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyoita nao hawakutaka kusikiliza, ndivyo walivyoita {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} sikutaka kusikiliza, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaita, lakini hawakutaka kusikiliza. Kwa hiyo walipolia kuomba msaada, sikuwasikiliza, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

ko.L: 그분께서 부르실 때 그들이 듣지 않았던 것처럼, 그들이 부를 때 나도 듣지 않았다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.B: 그분께서 부르셨을 때 그들이 듣지 않았듯이, 그들이 부르짖을 때 나도 듣지 않았다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들을 부르셨지만 그들은 듣지 않았다. 그러므로 그들이 부르짖을 때 나도 듣지 않았다. 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: he called ... I would not listen: the prophet's words become the LORD's own
decisions.reason: The verse begins by speaking of the LORD as "he" and ends with the LORD speaking as "I". Prophets often move from one to the other, because they speak for him.

decisions.choice: they would not listen, so I would not listen: the people received what they had given
decisions.reason: The same warning is in Proverbs 1:24-28, Jeremiah 11:11 and Micah 3:4: those who refuse to hear God's call will find that he does not answer their cry in the day of trouble.

decisions.choice: they called: in their distress, when disaster came
decisions.reason: The verb form often looks to the future, but here it tells what used to happen, as the story of the past goes on into verse 14.

decisions.choice: he, with the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: "He" is the LORD, so it takes the setting for pronouns of God. Readable names the LORD at the start to make the change of speaker clear.

decisions.choice: "dice" at every level
decisions.reason: The verb here is amar ("says"), not ne'um, so it is "dice" at every level, as the English has "says".

decisions.choice: "그분께서 부르실" with -시-, then "나도" without it
decisions.reason: The verse turns from the prophet speaking about God to God speaking (meaning decision); Korean marks the turn with the honorific, which God never uses of himself.

decisions.choice: "CHÚA Vạn Quân phán" at every level for 'amar YHWH tseva'ot
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "phán vậy" (L, B) for ne'um and plain "phán" at every level for 'amar.

source.text: וְאֵ֣סָעֲרֵ֗ם עַ֤ל כָּל־הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־יְדָע֔וּם וְהָאָ֨רֶץ֙ נָשַׁ֣מָּה אַֽחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם מֵֽעֹבֵ֖ר וּמִשָּׁ֑ב וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ אֶֽרֶץ־חֶמְדָּ֖ה לְשַׁמָּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And I stormed them away among all the nations whom not they had known, and the land was desolate behind them, from passing through and from returning; and they made a land of delight into a desolation.

en.L: And I scattered them with a storm among all the nations whom they had not known; and the land behind them was left desolate, with no one coming or going; and they made the pleasant land a desolation.
en.B: I scattered them like a whirlwind among all the nations they had not known. The land they left behind was so desolate that no one came or went. They turned the pleasant land into a wasteland.
en.R: I scattered them like a storm scatters things, among nations they had never known. The land they left behind became so empty that no one came or went. They turned that beautiful land into a desert.

fr.L: Et je les ai dispersés dans la tempête parmi toutes les nations qu’ils ne connaissaient pas ; et le pays a été dévasté derrière eux, sans personne qui passe ni qui revienne ; et ils ont fait du pays de délices une désolation.
fr.B: Je les ai dispersés comme un tourbillon parmi toutes les nations qu’ils ne connaissaient pas. Le pays qu’ils ont laissé derrière eux est devenu si désolé que personne n’y passait plus. Ils ont fait de ce pays si beau un désert.
fr.R: Je les ai dispersés comme une tempête emporte tout, parmi des nations qu’ils ne connaissaient pas. Le pays qu’ils ont laissé est devenu si vide que plus personne n’y allait ni n’en venait. Ils ont transformé ce beau pays en désert.

es.L: Y los esparcí con torbellino entre todas las naciones que ellos no habían conocido; y la tierra quedó desolada tras ellos, sin nadie que pasara ni volviera; y convirtieron la tierra deseable en desolación.
es.B: Los dispersé como un torbellino entre todas las naciones que no conocían. La tierra que dejaron quedó tan desolada que nadie iba ni venía por ella. Convirtieron la tierra hermosa en una desolación.
es.R: Los dispersé como la tormenta dispersa las cosas, entre naciones que nunca habían conocido. La tierra que dejaron quedó tan vacía que nadie iba ni venía. Convirtieron aquella tierra hermosa en un desierto.

vi.L: Ta đã dùng bão tố đùa chúng đi giữa mọi dân tộc mà chúng không biết; và đất bị bỏ hoang sau khi chúng đi, không ai qua lại; và chúng đã biến xứ tốt đẹp thành nơi hoang vu.
vi.B: Ta đã làm cho chúng tan tác như cơn gió lốc giữa mọi dân tộc chúng chưa từng biết. Đất chúng bỏ lại hoang tàn đến nỗi không ai qua lại. Chúng đã biến xứ tốt đẹp thành nơi hoang vu.
vi.R: Ta đã làm cho họ tan lạc như cơn bão cuốn đi mọi vật, đến giữa những dân tộc họ chưa từng biết. Đất họ bỏ lại trở nên trống vắng đến nỗi không ai qua lại. Họ đã biến xứ xinh đẹp ấy thành hoang mạc.

sw.L: Nami nikawatawanya kwa dhoruba kati ya mataifa yote ambayo hawakuyajua; na nchi ikabaki ukiwa nyuma yao, bila mtu kupita wala kurudi; nao wakaifanya nchi ya kupendeza kuwa ukiwa.
sw.B: Niliwatawanya kama kimbunga kati ya mataifa yote wasiyoyajua. Nchi waliyoiacha nyuma ikawa ukiwa kiasi kwamba hakuna aliyekwenda wala kurudi. Waliigeuza nchi ya kupendeza kuwa jangwa.
sw.R: Niliwatawanya kama dhoruba inavyotawanya vitu, kati ya mataifa ambayo hawakuwahi kuyajua. Nchi waliyoiacha ikawa tupu kabisa, hata hakuna mtu aliyepita huko. Waliigeuza nchi ile nzuri kuwa jangwa.

ko.L: 내가 그들을 그들이 알지 못하던 모든 민족들 가운데로 폭풍으로 흩어 버렸고, 그들이 떠난 뒤 그 땅은 황폐하여 오가는 자가 없었다. 그들이 그 아름다운 땅을 황무지로 만든 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 그들을 회오리바람처럼 그들이 알지 못하던 모든 민족들 가운데로 흩어 버렸다. 그들이 떠난 뒤 그 땅은 황폐해져서 오가는 사람이 없었다. 그들이 그 아름다운 땅을 황무지로 만든 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 폭풍이 모든 것을 날려 버리듯 그들을 그들이 알지 못하던 나라들 가운데로 흩어 버렸다. 그들이 떠난 뒤 그 땅은 텅 비어 아무도 오가지 않았다. 그들이 그 아름다운 땅을 사막으로 만든 것이다.

decisions.choice: I scattered them with a storm: drove them away as a whirlwind blows things away
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a storm or whirlwind (Habakkuk 3:14). The exile swept the people away suddenly and far.

decisions.choice: with no one coming or going: no traffic at all
decisions.reason: "Passing through and returning" means people traveling back and forth. The land was empty of all travelers (Ezekiel 35:7).

decisions.choice: the pleasant land: the land God gave as a treasure
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in Jeremiah 3:19 ("a pleasant land, the most beautiful heritage") and Psalm 106:24. The people's own sin turned the land of delight into a wasteland. Chapter 8 turns from this past to the promise of what the LORD will now do.

decisions.choice: like a whirlwind (B); like a storm scatters things (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the picture in the verb into a comparison. "Pleasant land" (L, B) becomes "beautiful land" (R).

decisions.choice: "la tierra deseable" (L); "la tierra hermosa" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The pleasant land is "la tierra hermosa" at B and R, as Daniel 11:16 in Spanish; L keeps "deseable" for the Hebrew "land of delight".
